fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The mural that started the bloodline hunt", "body": "Clint Richardson traces his genealogy research back to Dr. A. True Ott of Mother Earth Minerals, who took him to the Mormon Genealogical Center in Utah. On the wall was a mural running from Anne Hutchinson, the accused Salem witch, down through Joseph Smith, George Bush, Mitt Romney, Churchill and a president of Ireland. Richardson tells Chance Garton that the sheer accuracy of the Latter day Saints record keeping, and the fact that everyone important sat on one family chart, sent him into months of addictive genealogical study he could not stop."}, {"title": "Cousins running against cousins", "body": "Richardson argues this is not the Kevin Bacon parlor game of distant relation. He says England's main genealogical firm has predicted American presidents for two hundred years by checking royal descent, that George Bush and John Kerry are ninth cousins once removed and both descend from Vlad the Impaler through the kings of England, and that Obama comes through a white Connecticut landholding family. He cites a Newsweek piece claiming fifty of the hundred senators were Obama's cousins. The point, he insists, is direct line of succession, not cousinship, and it extends to CEOs and Hollywood actors."}, {"title": "How the nation state conquered every country", "body": "The core of Richardson's newer work is the Treaty of Westphalia and what followed. Countries were turned into republics, then handed Masonic constitutions, then recognized internationally as nation states. He tells Chance that California, England and Scotland are not sovereign states in any international sense, that only the United States and the United Kingdom are, and that the United Nations definition requires conquering the people of the territory you claim. Purchase, he says, is just voluntary conquest. The Lieber Code, military bases in every state and the Fourteenth Amendment complete the picture of an occupied and indentured population."}, {"title": "Res publica, the Rasenna and the wisdom cult", "body": "Chance Garton takes the word republic back past Latin to the Etruscans, whose priest class called themselves the Rasenna, arguing that ras means head and wisdom, so res publica means the head of the public. He links this to the Greek archon and to Barashit in Genesis, which he reads as by wisdom God created. From there he sketches the College of Alexandria sending out therapeutes, Essenes, ascetics and Pythagoreans as one order under many names, the guarded doctrine of the seculum, and the Neros cycle, which he jokes has resurfaced today as nepo babies."}, {"title": "Why the truth movement is a worse lie", "body": "Richardson is blunt that the patriot movement he helped build is a simulation. He breaks patriot into pat riot, a riot that does nothing, calls the private membership association boom a confidence game recycled from the tax protest movement, and warns that the paperwork only kicks the lien down the road. He describes losing six months of genealogy files to something that corrupted only those documents, and having lethal injection scrubbed from YouTube. Chance offers biofield tuning as a way to drop conditioned beliefs, and Richardson closes by proposing a religion of non belief."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Reality researcher and patriot myth-buster Clint Richardson returns to InnerVerse for his fifth appearance. Join us for a discussion on the occulted royal bloodline that permeates all influential institutions of western civilization, from Hollywood celebrities to political figureheads. We will also delve into Clint's most recent realizations about how to utilize true privacy in the legal sense, to avoid the detrimental "rights" that are inflicted on the public person.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Public Person And The Private Man", "body": "Clint's central distinction in the second half is that the citizen is a status, not a self. The birth certificate, he argues, is an indenture that domiciles you in the United States while leaving you a mere resident of the state you actually live in, so the person carries the taxes, the consumer protections and the accounting while you serve as its agent. He compares it to picking a piece on a monopoly board, where the shoe collects every penalty and benefit but somebody real is moving it. Acting privately, in his framing, simply means declining to play that piece."}, {"title": "Contract As The Machinery Of Consent", "body": "Much of the exclusive hour turns on agreements nobody reads. Clint walks through the end user agreement on a computer, which he says quietly moves you out of your own legal system and into arbitration chosen by the other side, and connects it to what he calls the doctrine of master and servant hiding inside the word volunteer. A listener in the live chat notices that end user sounds like indenture, and Clint runs with it, describing a performance debt rather than a monetary one, an apprenticeship whose terms you agreed to by signing the authorized signature printed inside what looks like a dotted line."}, {"title": "Private Associations Run The Public World", "body": "Clint argues the visible government is downstream of invisible clubs. He describes walking into the Mormon church's corporate offices in Utah asking for financial statements and being told they are private and not bound to share anything, which set him looking at the corporation sole, the model he says the Crown uses as it travels from country to country. From there he maps the National Governors Association copyrighting Common Core, the Uniform Law Commission drafting roughly a hundred and twenty uniform laws, and the international version in Rome, all passing policy state by state without anything being passed federally."}, {"title": "The Guru Economy And Its Red Flags", "body": "Asked directly for warning signs, Clint gives a list. There is no such thing as a state national. A non citizen passport is a federal crime, not a loophole. A 508 is not a status you can hold without first being a 501c3. Above all, he says, be suspicious of anyone steering you away from the government's own form, because clerks are required to file whatever arrives, the fraudulent filing sits quietly for years, and the tax lien lands long after the guru is gone. His summary line is competence over confidence, and never buy somebody else's paperwork."}, {"title": "Time, Money And The Things We Agree To Believe", "body": "The conversation widens into what the two of them think holds the whole arrangement together. Clint says he stopped believing in time altogether, then shows why it matters legally, since a contract's time is its life and a bank's thirty day demand only bites because you accept the clock. Chance offers the Greek distinction between measured time and the subjective kind, suggesting real time is the growth between one phase of life and the next. Clint sets the gurus' promised redemption beside it as another pot of gold at the end of a rainbow that recedes forever."}]
